scope: Rexonance assembly preparation, futuristic typography and control feedback
implementation: Driver, raw-gold and unlit intermediate canvases select willReadFrequently on their first context, before drawing decoded artwork.
A temporary alpha-compositing parity probe enables CPU preparation only on byte-compatible backends; its five small stores are released and only a boolean is cached per document.
Compatible CPU row work uses a 2.5 ms cooperative budget instead of 1.5 ms; legacy fallback remains at 1.5 ms. Idle deadline checks, cancellation and live rendering are unchanged.

Japanese display type uses local gothic and Latin display type uses the existing self-hosted Forge face. Two unused Mincho preloads totalling 10300 bytes are removed; original artwork and copy are preserved.

Controls have 140 ms press feedback and a visible keyboard focus outline. Motion stays disabled in reduced-motion, economy and forced-colors modes. Existing pointer contact state is reused without adding gesture handlers.

Native chapter-link clicks re-resolve their target once on the next frame to avoid stale post-rotation WebKit geometry. Hash/history/focus remain native; fresh input or page disposal cancels pending work, with no scroll listener or continuous animation loop.

timing.network: Loopback production builds, browser cache disabled, no bandwidth throttle
timing.measurement: After hydration, load and scroll restoration settle, scroll to 423 px (half-viewport preparation threshold); stop at data-rzn-load=ready.
timing.method: Five fresh contexts per build, alternating AB/BA. Byte hashing runs separately from timing.
timing.qualification: CPU backing alone did not reduce ready time in this environment; the reported improvement is the combined CPU-backed and bounded-batching implementation. The reported 7 s preparation and 1.2 s GPU stalls were not reproduced locally.

byteParity.chrome: All ordered SHA-256 byte digests exactly equal main; all five instrumented readback sources CPU-backed.
byteParity.webkit: WebKit 26.5 detects different alpha rounding and retains legacy stores. All ordered SHA-256 byte digests exactly equal main.

verification.zenith: Passed 43 observations: phone390 forward/reverse, reduced motion, Save-Data, 2G, WebKit native and no-scroll-timeline fallback.
verification.renderContracts: Touch art <=64 draws, <=16 nanite sprites, allocation-free draw passes and distant prefetch presentation pins passed.
verification.typography: Chrome and WebKit at 320/390/1024/1440: no horizontal overflow or dormant Mincho requests; keyboard navigation/focus and normal/reduced/economy press states passed.
verification.operability: Chrome passed all eight profiles. WebKit passed seven of eight; tablet-portrait retains the baseline Option-Tab landing failure recorded below. Native visible links and real narrow-screen drawer links are exercised, with unchanged arrival and focus tolerances.
verification.interactionEdges: All five profiles passed, including 320 px, touch cancellation, menu scrolling/swiping, dialogs, delayed artwork, Back and Zeus return cleanup.
verification.release: Five SPA departures after adding the anchor correction, including stalled image requests and Back under the entry cover: zero retained page nodes and zero detached main nodes.
verification.performance: Existing performance verifier passed; repeated selected-tab presses and 60 hero scroll changes cause zero Rexonance React commits.

knownIssues.scope: WebKit 26.5 automated keyboard navigation, 1024x1366 touch profile
knownIssues.symptom: Option-Tab from the P14 range focuses the correct #stages assembly-guide link but does not bring it into the viewport.
knownIssues.status: Reproduced on both builds; not introduced or repaired by this preparation/typography change. Physical-device behavior remains unverified.

knownIssues.scope: WebKit programmatic fragment assignment after rotation
knownIssues.symptom: Directly assigning location.hash can retain an incorrect native destination after rotation. The operability verifier now exercises the actual drawer links at narrow widths, including their existing router and scroll-lock release behavior.
knownIssues.status: The new one-frame correction covers native chapter-link clicks, not unrelated programmatic hash assignments or history restoration.

limitations: These are local production-build measurements, not public-network or physical-device measurements.
Physical iPhone/iPad and iPadOS 27.2 home-screen mode were not tested.
WebKit preserves the exact existing output through fallback; this report does not claim a WebKit preparation speedup.
The measured 6 ms slice target is not a hard wall-clock guarantee on arbitrary hardware.
